text:
Anton Lundell missed Saturday in Washington with an undisclosed injury, came back for the afternoon in Boston, put five shots on Jeremy Swayman and still went home without a point. That has been his autumn. He has 6 points in 17 games, and if you strip out the hat trick against Winnipeg on Oct. 30, his last ten games hold nothing at all.

Our read is that most of this is bad luck rather than bad hockey. Florida has scored 6.0 fewer goals than its chances deserve with Lundell on the ice, and the Panthers take almost 56% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) when he plays at five on five, about five points better than without him. That is a two-time Stanley Cup winner doing his job against top competition, which Evolving-Hockey had in the 90th percentile last season.

His points rate sits at 1.2 per 60 minutes; our range for his true talent runs from 1.6 to 2.3. We project 42 more points. Watch whether the on-ice goals start arriving now that he's back from the injury.
headline: The goals went missing, not the game
